# grid.Body's row and column windows need clone descriptors, so two grids stop sharing one window

## Context

The operator-reported symptom from #18186 is still live: on the Workstation's 100k Matrix, `+1 pulse` increments the record and never repaints the cell, for every row below the sixth.

#18186 was dropped as Drop+Supersede because it was scoped as a grid bug when the mechanism sits in the config system, and two fixes of mine were dropped with it — a `construct()` copy (#18190) and a move to instance fields (#18191). @tobiu's ruling on the shape: *"if the [config system] does not honor NEO BEST PRACTISES, like core.Config and config descriptors ... it is a failure. using config descriptors e.g. inside grid body => that is fine."*

So: the config-system gap is D#18195 / #18192. **This ticket is the consumer fix, done the Neo-native way** — with descriptors, not with a hand-rolled copy and not by leaving the config system.

## The Problem

`src/grid/Body.mjs` declares `mountedRows`, `visibleRows` and `visibleColumns` in `static config` as non-reactive array literals, and both window calculators write through them by index (`me.mountedRows[0] = mountedStart` — the source says `// update the array inline`).

A non-reactive key has no clone path, so every grid body on a page holds the same array. The Workstation renders two grids: the feed grid (`availableRows 1`, `bufferRowRange 2`) writes a 5-row window into the array the scale grid (`availableRows 7`, `bufferRowRange 10`) is reading, so the scale grid believes 6 of its 27 painted rows are mounted.

Both repaint paths gate on that window and treat anything outside it as nothing to do — `onStoreRecordChange()` skips the row, `getRow()` returns `null`, and `AnimatedChange` no-ops under its `if (row)`. Nothing warns. The store stays correct, so only the paint is missing.

Measured on the running app: calling `updateMountedAndVisibleRows()` on the **scale** body alone moved the **feed** body's window from `[0,5]` to `[0,27]` — a window its own geometry cannot produce.

## The Fix

Declare the three as reactive configs carrying a descriptor:

```javascript
mountedRows_: {
    [isDescriptor]: true,
    clone         : 'shallow',
    cloneOnGet    : 'none',
    value         : [0, 0]
},
```

Both keys of the descriptor are load-bearing, and the pairing was measured at `core.Base` before being applied here:

| descriptor | same-instance identity | two instances | after `a[0] = 99` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `clone:'none', cloneOnGet:'none'` | stable | **shared** | sibling `[99,0]`, class default `[99,0]` |
| `clone:'deep', cloneOnGet:'none'` | stable | isolated | sibling `[0,0]` |
| **`clone:'shallow', cloneOnGet:'none'`** | **stable** | **isolated** | `a` `[99,0]`, sibling `[0,0]`, default clean |

- **`clone: 'shallow'`** copies the declared default on set, so each body gets its own two-element array. `'deep'` would work identically for an array of numbers and costs more; `'none'` reproduces the defect exactly.
- **`cloneOnGet: 'none'`** is what makes an index-write land. Without it the getter copies arrays on every read — the engine's default for reactive array configs — so `me.mountedRows[0] = x` would write into a discarded copy and the window would never move at all. This is a **behaviour-critical** pairing, not a performance tweak.

`mountedColumns_` is already reactive in this class, so the shape has precedent three lines away.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — every row rendered in the visible area increments its own Pulse cell, asserted by record id against the running app.
- [ ] **AC-2** — red-first at exact head: the e2e witness fails on records 7-27 before the change and passes after, and the unit isolation arms fail before and pass after. The absence of the fix is asserted (`grep`), not assumed from a `git stash`.
- [ ] **AC-3** — two grid bodies with **unequal** geometry hold different window arrays and neither can move the other's. Equal geometries produce equal windows and would pass while still sharing.
- [ ] **AC-4** — an index-write through `me.mountedRows[0]` is still observable on the instance after the change. This is what `cloneOnGet: 'none'` buys and it must have its own arm: a getter that copies silently reverts every window update.
- [ ] **AC-5** — a recycled row after scrolling acts on the record it currently displays.
- [ ] **AC-6** — no `NEO_TEST_SKIP_CI` guard on the new arms. The `unit` job sets it, so a guarded regression arm is green in CI by not running.
- [ ] **AC-7** — the full unit suite stays green at exact head.

## Out of Scope

- **The config-system defect** — that a `clone` descriptor is silently inert on a *non-reactive* key. That is #18192, diverging in D#18195, and this ticket must not be used to pressure that fork toward whichever option unblocks the grid. This fix works under every option on that matrix, because it moves the keys onto the reactive path where descriptors already work.
- A sweep of the other in-place-mutated non-reactive configs. 38 candidates surfaced; each needs per-class confirmation that the key has no reactive ancestor and the class is genuinely multi-instance. Separate lane.

## Avoided Traps

- **Reassigning instead of writing through.** `src/grid/Container.mjs` destructures `{mountedColumns, visibleColumns}` off the body and mutates through the reference; switching to reassignment would strand that consumer on a stale array. Caught by @neo-opus-grace on #18190.
- **Omitting `cloneOnGet: 'none'`.** The most likely way to get this wrong, and it fails silently in the same direction as the original bug.
- **Instance fields.** They work, and @tobiu ruled the descriptor route is the one that honours the config system.

## Timeline

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-09-03T11:25:44Z

**Blocked-by (soft) on D#18195 Option F — and the fix shrinks to three characters if F lands.**

@tobiu's ruling while this ticket was being written: *"the goal is to NOT create more boilerplate, but finding the sweet spot that results in LESS loc."*

This ticket as filed adds three explicit `{clone: 'shallow', cloneOnGet: 'none'}` descriptors to `src/grid/Body.mjs` — about **18 lines of boilerplate**, which is the direction that ruling goes against.

A sweep of every descriptor in `src/` found the reason: **four classes have already hand-written the same pair to opt out of the engine defaults** — `container/Base.mjs` `items_`, `selection/Model.mjs` `items_`, `tab/Container.mjs` `headerActions_` (all three `clone: 'shallow'` + `cloneOnGet: 'none'`), and `collection/Base.mjs` `items_` (`clone: 'shallow'`, added specifically because `clone: 'deep'` was deep-cloning a 50 000-record collection). Adding a fifth copy is the wrong move; four sites sharing one idiom is a missing default.

So the two lanes are **ordered, not independent**:

- **F lands first** → this fix is adding one underscore to each of three config keys. The windows become reactive, get a per-instance array on construction and a stable reference on read, both by default. Roughly **−18 lines** versus the approach in the body above.
- **F does not land** → the descriptor approach in this ticket is correct and stays as the fallback.

The measured pairing in the ticket body is unchanged and still the reason `cloneOnGet: 'none'` is behaviour-critical rather than cosmetic: without it the getter copies on every read and an index-write lands in a discarded copy, so the window never moves.

Holding rather than shipping the boilerplate version. The operator-reported symptom is live, and that pressure is exactly what would otherwise push the wrong shape through — which is how the three predecessors (#18186, #18190, #18191) got dropped.
